reviewerOrPass: Worker B, same AI, separate source-first pass
method: After freezing and replaying the decision and canonical record, reread the programme-specific 2026–27 regulations, major annexes, student curriculum and thesis guidance. Reconstructed the 127.5 plus 52.5 EC example and checked the grammar test, writing progression and linked corpus and thesis sequence. Reconsidered the exact workbook evidence for practical Dutch, comparative literary work, language acquisition, rhetoric and digital methods against the three finished options and revised alignment. This is a separate same-AI pass.
findings: The programme-specific 2026–2027 regulations confirm the full-time Dutch Language and Culture bachelor. The example preserves the fully Dutch-taught subject-specific track: 127.5 EC major plus 52.5 EC profiling. The major combines two 30 EC base packages, a 30 EC depth package, two shared advanced courses totaling 15 EC, a 7.5 EC methods choice, a 7.5 EC corpus course and a 7.5 EC thesis in Dutch. The level-3 depth package and shared advanced courses provide 45 EC even before the corpus course and thesis, satisfying the advanced major floor. The profiling allocation includes a 30 EC coherent package. Crossing Borders is separately formal, has a 135 EC major and may teach up to one third in English. The first-listed language package and methods option are retained independently of UCR fit.

The regulations distinguish the 2026–27 intake from transitional curricula and prescribe a compulsory zero-credit basic grammar test. The student guide positions two base packages before the depth package and identifies writing development across the degree. The corpus course is offered in block 2 or 3 and prepares the supervised 7.5 EC final thesis in Dutch. The thesis follows this preparation and may be scheduled in any block subject to registration. Electives include a coherent 30 EC package chosen from the approved options, with prior permission for external or international selections. The reviewed comparison shows the curriculum rather than certifying an individual timetable.

The broad plan balances literary reading, style, rhetoric, psycholinguistics, media, social identity and qualitative and historical research. The language option emphasizes language acquisition and processing, public rhetoric, social and digital discourse, AI ethics and language-model technology. Mathematical Methods supplies a required gateway for Neural Networks & Deep Learning. Public rhetoric offers direct community-engaged communication, and the introductory Dutch course supports practical use rather than advanced language analysis. The literature option adds myth, reception, adaptation, cultural institutions, museum and art-historical interpretation and documentary work. These are sustained approaches with materially different 180 EC compositions, not Dutch philology sequences. Psycholinguistics supports acquisition and processing across languages based on the actual description. General text data, media identity and historical methods are relevant complements but cannot be paired as substantive matches to Dutch corpus tools, Dutch identity, or medieval and early modern Dutch texts. Dedicated Dutch-language depth, comparative Dutch linguistics, multilingual literacy and the compulsory Dutch thesis remain gaps. The official Crossing Borders track was considered and remains represented in candidate evidence; the retained three options cover the broad and two department-level interests within the three-option maximum. UCR optional independent research is 15 EC outside the scheduled degree, distinct from Utrecht’s required 7.5 EC thesis.
